Use N-mm-MPa as the unit system throughout. Apply Euler-Bernoulli beam theory with linear elastic, small-deflection assumptions.
Model a cantilever beam fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L = 1800 mm.
The beam has a constant flexural rigidity with E = 200000 MPa and I = 1200000 mm^4.
A single downward point load P = 2000 N is applied at the free end (x = L). No other loads, supports, or applied couples exist.
The internal bending moment varies linearly as M(x) = P(L - x), giving M(0) = PL at the fixed end and M(L) = 0 at the free end.
Compute the free-end slope using θ = P*L^2 / (2*E*I), reporting the result in radians. If convenient, also append the equivalent value in degrees.
Compute the free-end vertical deflection using δ = P*L^3 / (3*E*I), reporting the result in mm, with the direction stated as downward.
Present both results rounded to three or four significant figures.
